lesson.subject: science
lesson.title: Rocks, Fossils and Soils
lesson.summary: Types of rock, how they wear away, how fossils form and what soil is made of.
learning_objectives: Explain weathering, erosion and fossil formation
Describe what soil is made of

standards.text: Compare and group rocks based on appearance and physical properties; describe how fossils are formed; recognise that soils are made from rocks and organic matter

success_criteria: I can tell natural rock from human-made materials
I can explain how a fossil forms
I can say what soil is made of
lesson.real_life: Spotting rocks on a walk, finding fossils on a beach and caring for garden soil.

blocks.markdown: Today we explore **rocks**, fossils and soil.
blocks.say: Welcome, young scientist! Today we sort rocks, find out how fossils form, and look at what soil is made of.

blocks.markdown: **Rock** is a natural material found in the Earth.
blocks.say: Rock is a natural material found in the Earth. People dig it from the ground in quarries.
Brick, concrete and tarmac are not rock. People make them in factories. Rocks such as granite, chalk, slate, marble and sandstone are all natural.

scenes.caption: Natural rocks.
scenes.say: Granite, chalk and slate come from the ground. They are natural rocks.

scenes.caption: Human-made materials.
scenes.say: Brick and tarmac are made by people. They are not rocks.

question.prompt: Which of these is a natural rock?
question.explanation: Slate is a natural rock. Brick and concrete are made by people.

blocks.markdown: A **hard** rock is difficult to scratch.
blocks.say: We describe rocks by their properties. Some are hard and some are soft. A hard rock does not scratch easily.

blocks.markdown:
A **permeable** rock lets water soak in.

An **impermeable** rock does not.
blocks.say: Some rocks are permeable. They let water soak into them. Impermeable rocks do not.

blocks.alt: Permeable rocks let water soak in.
blocks.caption: Permeable rocks let water soak in.

question.prompt: Granite is a hard rock that water does not soak into easily.

blocks.title: A shell in the cliff
blocks.transcript: Millions of years ago, a shelled animal lives in a warm sea. It dies and sinks to the sea floor. Mud and sand cover it. Layer on layer builds up. Over a long time, the layers turn to rock. The shell leaves a fossil in the rock. It stays there for millions of years. Wind, rain and frost weather the cliff. The rock crumbles into pieces. A river carries bits away. They mix with humus to make soil. A girl finds the fossil in the cliff, just like Mary Anning did. Now the fossil sits in a museum. It tells us about life long ago.
blocks.caption: A fossil shell tells its journey from sea creature to museum.

points: Rocks can be hard or soft, permeable or not
blocks.say: Remember. Rock is natural. Brick and tarmac are not. We describe rocks by hardness and permeability.

blocks.markdown: The **scratch test** shows which rock is harder.
blocks.say: To test hardness, scratch one rock with another. The rock that leaves a scratch on the other is harder.

blocks.markdown: Keep the number of drops the same for a **fair test**.
blocks.say: To test permeability, drip the same number of drops on each rock. Watch which rock soaks up water fastest.

blocks.markdown: A **fossil** is the remains or imprint of a living thing in rock.
blocks.say: A fossil is the remains or imprint of a living thing, preserved in rock. Fossils tell us about life from long ago.

blocks.alt: Fossils of ancient animals pressed into grey rock
blocks.caption: Trilobite fossils in rock.
blocks.credit: Photo by Wes Warren on Unsplash
blocks.say: These fossils are ancient sea animals called trilobites. They were buried in mud, and over millions of years the mud turned to rock.

scenes.caption: Buried in sediment.
scenes.say: A sea creature dies and sinks to the sea floor. Mud and sand called sediment cover it.

scenes.caption: Pressed into rock.
scenes.say: Over a very long time, the layers press down and turn to rock. The shell leaves a fossil.

question.prompt: What covers a dead sea creature when it begins to form a fossil?

blocks.title: Fossil match
blocks.say: Flip the cards and find the matching pairs. A little brain break!

blocks.markdown: **Mary Anning** found fossils on the Dorset coast.
blocks.say: Mary Anning lived in Lyme Regis in Dorset, about two hundred years ago. As a girl, she found huge fossils in the cliffs.

blocks.alt: Spiral ammonite fossils in grey rock beside sand
blocks.caption: Ammonite fossils in rock.
blocks.credit: Photo by Ashleigh Joy Photography on Unsplash
blocks.say: This rock holds ammonite fossils, ancient spiral-shelled sea animals. Fossils are rare, because most living things rot away.

question.prompt: Every living thing that dies becomes a fossil.
question.explanation: Most living things rot away. Fossils form only in special conditions.

points: A fossil is the remains or imprint of a living thing
blocks.say: Remember. Fossils form when living things are buried and turn to rock. Any living thing can become a fossil.

blocks.markdown: **Soil** is made of rock pieces, **humus**, water and air.
blocks.say: Soil is made of tiny pieces of rock, humus, water and air. Humus is rotted dead plants and animals.

blocks.alt: Hands pressing dark garden soil around tiny green seedlings
blocks.caption: Soil is full of rock pieces and humus.
blocks.credit: Photo by Sandie Clarke on Unsplash
blocks.say: Soil takes a very long time to form. Sandy soil has big grains and drains fast. Clay soil has tiny grains and holds water.

question.explanation: Humus is decayed plant and animal matter.

options.text: Rotted dead plants and animals in soil

blocks.say: Weathering breaks rock into smaller pieces. Rain, wind, ice and plant roots can all do this.
Erosion carries those pieces away. Rivers carry silt that makes rich farmland, such as along the Indus.

scenes.caption: Weathering breaks rock.
scenes.say: Rain and frost break a rock into small pieces. That is weathering.

scenes.caption: Erosion carries pieces away.
scenes.say: A river carries the pieces downstream. That is erosion.

blocks.prompt: How could farmers protect soil from being washed away? Have a think first.
blocks.answer_markdown: Plant trees and grass, cover bare ground, and use terraces. Roots hold the soil in place.

blocks.say: Remember. Soil is rock pieces and humus. Weathering breaks rock. Erosion carries it away. We must protect soil.

terms.meaning: A mixture of rock pieces, humus, water and air.
